Content: A note on the sponsor: I work for an MSP. We use ThreatLocker and we deploy it to our clients. It is the worst piece of software I have ever used. There have been several cases, such as simply connecting to a printer hosted on a print server, which have been stopped by ThreatLocker and it wasn't apparent that was the cause until way more troubleshooting time than necessary. I'm not a security guy but when the "security" product impacts peoples' abilities to do their work, it's not a good product. I'm sure all whitelist/zero trust style of security applications have the same fault but I'm only familiar with ThreatLocker. Unless your company has a well staffed security team to sift through hundreds of application requests, I'd suggest staying far away from ThreatLocker.

Author: @uniquenameidentifier3045
Content:
You can connect Macs directly with Thunderbolt, so you can bring something like the iodyne Pro Data instead of that NAS/Ethernet adapter/Ubiquiti switch combo. It has slots for twelve M.2 NVMe SSDs and eight Thunderbolt 3 ports (four upstream and four downstream).

That means you can hook up many editors to this thing directly with Multi-Reader Sharing that ensures "data discipline" across multiple users (avoiding duplicate copies and versions of assets, protects against the risk of overwriting OCFs and OCNs or corrupting files, and the overall messiness that comes with large data sets) at up to 5GB/s speeds. This thing is built exactly for what you are trying to accomplish here. It's an on-set device for editing on the go.

Also it fits in a normal backpack measuring 39.1cm × 25.4cm × 3.1cm and weighing 3.3kg.

You can connect the Mac mini directly with a USB4 cable to that NAS and forego that clunky ethernet adapter or add the $99 upgrade 10Gbps ethernet port to the Mac mini.

Author: @NoahtheGameplayer
Content:
The transcript describes the process of building a portable, high-performance storage and editing solution for the Consumer Electronics Show (CES). The team previously struggled with slow hotel internet in Las Vegas, which forced them to edit footage on location. To solve this, they built a compact and powerful NAS (Network-Attached Storage) system using a Mini PC, high-capacity SSDs, and fast networking hardware. The system is designed to be portable, fitting into a carry-on bag, and is equipped with enough storage and processing power to handle the large amounts of video footage generated during the event.

Key features of the setup include:

- *Hardware:* A Mini PC (ms01) with a Core i9-13900H processor, 96GB of DDR5 RAM, and high-capacity SSDs (two 8TB Sabrent Rocket 4 Plus drives in a mirrored configuration for redundancy).
- *Networking:* Dual 10GbE SFP+ ports and additional USB 4 ports for high-speed data transfer.
- *Storage:* Three M.2 slots for SSDs, with a focus on high-speed, high-capacity storage.
- *Editing Setup:* A Mac Mini M4 for editing, with the option to use a Windows VM for backup editing purposes.
- *Remote Access:* A Nano KVM for remote management of the system.
- *Proxies:* The team plans to use proxy files for editing and then conform the final video with raw footage on location.

The transcript also mentions the challenges of hotel internet in Las Vegas and the team's strategy to mitigate these issues by using local storage and editing on site. Additionally, the team promotes their sponsor, ThreatLocker, and their Zero Trust World event, offering a discount code for registration.

Overall, the transcript provides a detailed look at the technical setup and planning that goes into covering a major tech event like CES, with a focus on ensuring that the team can edit and produce content efficiently, even in less-than-ideal conditions.

Author: @jacewallace5552
Content:
bull on the macmini. You can get a beelink ser8 8845hs, 32GB ram, 1TB of storage for $100 less than a macmini. That's an EQUAL processor (depending on single core or multi core benchmarks) twice the ram and 4x the storage. It also has 4usbA (instead of ALL usbCs) 1usbc, 2 HDMI, 1 LAN, and it's dead silent. It's IGPU is great and you can emulate ps3/360/wiiU games at high frame rates and even play something like CS2 at 80FPS at 1080p. The macmini is an absolute ripoff compared to the beelink. I like how they talk about "how it would cost so much more if you upgraded from the m4" when it couldn't be further from the truth. To get a macmini at 32GB of ram and 1TB of storage, it would cost $1500. That's $1000 more than the beelink at the same specs.

For $1500, you can get the beelink ser9 AI 9 HX 370, 196GB ram, and 8TB of storage for $1500. The HX370 is far superior to the m4, you get 6x as much ram and 8x as much storage for the same price as the macmini. Linus shilling the macmini is hilarious because he knows nothing about miniPCs.

Author: @TooLongLinkVideoSummarizer
Content:
Summary: Linus Tech Tips replaces their bulky, heavy portable editing NAS, used for events like CES, with a much smaller and lighter system based on the Minisforum MS-01 Mini PC. The new setup includes a high-performance Intel i9 CPU, 96GB of RAM, fast NVMe SSD storage, and a dedicated workstation GPU for backup rendering, plus a Mac Mini M4 for editing, all packed into a standard backpack. They also discuss the challenges of hotel internet in Las Vegas, their process for ingesting footage, and how they'll send proxy footage back to the main office for remote editing. The system runs TrueNAS and uses a NanoKVM for remote management.

Introduction [00:00:00]
Linus introduces the problem of slow hotel internet at tech events like CES, necessitating on-site editing.
The old portable NAS was too heavy, causing issues with air travel.
A new, smaller, and lighter system is introduced using the Minisforum MS-01 Mini PC.

Networking Capabilities [00:02:19]
The MS-01 features dual 10 gigabit SFP+ ports, dual 2.5 gigabit ports, and dual 40 gigabit USB4 ports.
The onboard 10 gigabit is sufficient, but faster connections are possible via adapters.

GPU [00:03:13]
The system includes a PCIe x16 slot (8 lanes active) for expansion.
An Nvidia Quadro P1000 is installed as a backup GPU for remote rendering.
The system supports up to an RTX 2000 Ada or an RTX 4000 SFF with a custom cooler.
A Mac Mini M4 will be the primary editing machine, outperforming the MS-01 even with a top-tier GPU.

RAM Installation [00:05:30]
The system is upgraded with 96GB of DDR5 5600MT/s SODIMM RAM from Mushkin.
The system’s fan can be removed without removing the heat sink.

CPU Repasting [00:06:42]
The stock thermal paste is replaced with PTM 7950 for better cooling, especially on the laptop chip.
The CPU is an Intel Core i9-13900H, a 14-core mobile chip with a max turbo power of 115W, though limited to 80W in the BIOS.
The thermal paste is applied as a solid that becomes liquid when heated, improving thermal transfer.

Storage [00:09:45]
The system has three M.2 storage slots.
Two 8TB Sabrent Rocket 4 Plus NVMe SSDs are used for project storage.
A 512GB Sabrent Rocket Gen 3 NVMe SSD is used as a boot drive.
An included M.2 to 2.5-inch adapter is available if a 2.5 SSD is needed.

Powering On and TrueNAS Setup [00:10:42]
The whole system (MS-01, Mac Mini, switch) is smaller than the previous NAS.
The system runs TrueNAS Scale.
Two 8TB drives are configured in a mirrored setup to ensure data redundancy.
The Windows 11 virtual machine with Premiere Pro is available for emergency rendering (plan C).

NanoKVM [00:12:18]
A NanoKVM is used for remote system management.
It provides remote access to the system's keyboard, video, and mouse functions.
It can be used for a hard restart.

Plan B for Editing [00:13:47]
The Mac Mini M4 is powerful enough to be used for editing on location if necessary.

Process for Ingesting Footage [00:14:17]
Footage is ingested to the NAS via a MacBook Pro with a 10 gigabit ethernet dongle, similar to the old workflow.

Hotel Internet in Vegas [00:14:39]
Hotel internet in Las Vegas is unreliable and slow due to lack of competition.
Hardwired jacks in hotel rooms have been removed, making internet access problematic.

Sending Footage Back to the Office [00:15:36]
Proxy footage will be sent back to the main office for remote editing.
Project files are sent back to Vegas and conformed to the raw footage.

Packing it Up [00:16:08]
The entire system fits into the LTT Commuter Backpack.
The full backpack weighs 24 lbs with a water bottle.
